SOURCE: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation. Shih-Yang Liu, Chien-Yi Wang, Hongxu Yin, Pavlo Molchanov, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Min-Hung Chen (NVIDIA, HKUST). "Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024" (arXiv:2402.09353v6, 9 Jul 2024). The PDF does NOT say "oral"; that claim is unsupported by the text.

COVERAGE: All 23 pages, 74,336 chars, text extraction clean. Pages 1-10 main text, read fully. Appendix read for Table 7 (p14), Table 15 (p22), and the hyperparameter tables only in part. I did not read the MT-Bench sample answers (Tables 13/14) or the per-benchmark LLaVA Table 12. References skimmed only. Pages 11-23 are references plus appendix.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- DoRA method: split each pretrained weight into a per-column magnitude vector m and a direction V. m is trainable and V is frozen. LoRA (B,A) updates only the direction. It merges into W before inference, so there is no extra latency.
  number: none
  setup: Eq. 5, Sec 4.1, p4. Init m=||W0||_c, V=W0, B=0 as in LoRA, so W'=W0 at the start.
  quote: "We then keep V frozen and m a trainable vector. The directional component is then updated through LoRA." and "DoRA can be merged with the pre-trained weight before inference, thereby not introducing any additional latency."
  where: p4
- Weight-decomposition analysis: the (dD, dM) correlation is positive for LoRA and negative for FT and DoRA.
  number: FT -0.62, DoRA -0.31, LoRA 0.83
  setup: VL-BART fine-tuned on four image-text tasks, query/value matrices, 4 checkpoints per method, across layers (Fig 2, p4). LoRA applied only to q/v, following Sung et al. 2022.
  quote: "both FT and DoRA exhibit negative correlation values of -0.62 and -0.31, respectively. In contrast, LoRA shows a positive correlation with a value of 0.83."
  where: p4
  Authors' reading: LoRA moves magnitude and direction proportionally and cannot make a slight direction change with a large magnitude change, or the reverse. This is stated as a suspicion, not proven. Quote: "We suspect that such limitation of LoRA might stem from the challenge of concurrent learning both magnitude and directional adaptation" (p3).
- Commonsense reasoning gains over LoRA, same rank.
  number: +3.7 (LLaMA-7B), +1.0 (13B), +2.1 (LLaMA2-7B), +4.4 (LLaMA3-8B). Table 1 averages: 7B 74.7 to 78.4; 13B 80.5 to 81.5; LLaMA2-7B 77.6 to 79.7; LLaMA3-8B 80.8 to 85.2.
  setup: 8 tasks (BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA). Training data from all 8 tasks merged, following Hu et al. 2023. Baseline numbers for LLaMA-7B/13B are copied from Hu et al. 2023. LoRA on LLaMA2/3 was run by the authors with Hu et al.'s hyperparameters. DoRA keeps LoRA's rank and changes only the learning rate. Table 8 (p15): rank 32, alpha 64, LR 1e-4 for LLaMA-7B. Params 0.84% against LoRA's 0.83%. The paper notes the "0.01%" parameter rise comes from the magnitude vectors.
  quote: "DoRA further enhances accuracy by 3.7%, outstripping ChatGPT's accuracy levels" and "DoRA consistently surpasses LoRA on both LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B by 2.1% and 4.4%, respectively."
  where: p5-6, Table 1
  Caveat: Table 1 gives LLaMA-7B DoRA 78.4 and LoRA 74.7. Table 6 lists 78.1 for the same row (rank 32, 0.84%). Table 7 also gives 78.1 for DoRA with the detach trick and 78.3 without. The two numbers are never reconciled in the text.
- Half-rank DoRA beats full-rank LoRA.
  number: +2.8 (7B), +1.0 (13B), +2.9 (LLaMA2-7B), +4.2 (LLaMA3-8B), at about half the trainable parameters (0.43% against 0.83% on 7B).
  setup: DoRA† = rank halved (Table 1, p6)
  quote: "DoRA† exceeds LoRA's performance on LLaMA-7B by 2.8%, on LLaMA-13B by 1%, on LLaMA2-7B by 2.9%, and on LLaMA3-8B by 4.2%, despite having only half as many trainable parameters as LoRA."
  where: p5
- Gradient-detach trick: treat the norm ||V+dV||_c as a constant, so it gets no gradient. This cuts training memory with almost no accuracy change.
  number: -24.4% memory on LLaMA-7B (37.3 GB to 28.2 GB, batch 16, accumulation 4); -12.4% on VL-BART (23.4 GB to 20.5 GB, batch 300). Accuracy on LLaMA-7B 78.3 to 78.1; VL-BART 77.3 to 77.4.
  setup: Eq. 11, Table 7 (appendix p14). All later experiments use the trick.
  quote: "the modification leads to a training memory reduction of approximately 24.4% in fine-tuning LLaMA and 12.4% in VL-BART" and "treating ||V + ∆V ||c in Eq. (5) as a constant, thereby detaching it from the gradient graph."
  where: p5 (Sec 4.3); p14 (Table 7)
  Note: the paper gives no figure for DoRA's overhead relative to plain LoRA. It reports no step-time or memory comparison against LoRA, only against its own un-detached variant.
- Rank robustness: DoRA is far better than LoRA at low rank on LLaMA-7B commonsense.
  number: LoRA r=8 40.74%, r=4 39.49%. DoRA r=8 77.96%, r=4 61.89%. Table 15 shows DoRA r=32 78.4, r=64 72.1 and LoRA r=64 65.8. Both methods drop at r=64.
  setup: LLaMA-7B, r in {4,8,16,32,64} (Fig 5, Table 15, p22)
  quote: "LoRA's average accuracies drop to 40.74% for r = 8 and 39.49% for r = 4. In contrast, DoRA retains a notable accuracy of 77.96% for r = 8 and 61.89% for r = 4"
  where: p8-9
  Caveat: the LoRA numbers at r=4, 8 and 64 (for example HellaSwag 11.8 and 17.6) look like unstable or failed runs. Single run per cell, no seeds reported. The paper does not discuss this.
- VL-BART multi-task: DoRA beats LoRA and roughly matches FT on image-text. On video-text it gains about 2 points but stays below FT on one task.
  number: Image-text average FT 77.3, LoRA 76.5, DoRA 77.4. Video-text average FT 87.5, LoRA 83.5, DoRA 85.4. YC2C is 154 for FT, 140.9 for LoRA and 145.4 for DoRA.
  setup: VL-BART with CLIP-ResNet101 and BART-base. LoRA and FT numbers are copied from Sung et al. 2022. Params 5.96% and 5.19%.
  quote: "DoRA exceeds LoRA's performance by nearly 1% in image-text understanding tasks, reaching the accuracy level of FT."
  where: p7 (Tables 2, 3)
- LLaVA-1.5-7B visual instruction tuning: DoRA 67.6, LoRA 66.9, FT 66.5.
  number: +0.7 over LoRA, +1.1 over FT, 7 benchmarks, 4.63% params.
  setup: LLaVA LoRA configuration, Table 4. The paper states the text "+0.6" in the intro against 0.7 in the body (67.6-66.9=0.7). The authors observe LoRA already beats FT here and suggest FT overfits.
  quote: "DoRA still demonstrates superior performance over both LoRA and FT, with an average improvement of 0.7% over LoRA and 1.1% over FT."
  where: p7
- DVoRA (DoRA plus VeRA) on MT-Bench, GPT-4 scored, Alpaca 10K subset, 80 questions.
  number: LLaMA-7B: LoRA 5.1, DoRA 5.5, VeRA 4.3, DVoRA 5.0 (0.04% params). LLaMA2-7B: LoRA 5.7, DoRA 6.0, VeRA 5.5, DVoRA 6.0.
  setup: Table 5, p8. Training-set-size sweep of 1000 to 10000 samples (Fig 4, Fig 9). DoRA ahead at every size.
  quote: "DV oRA outperforms VeRA by 0.7/0.5 points and achieves the same level of accuracy as LoRA on LLaMA-7B and DoRA on LLaMA2-7B, respectively."
  where: p8
- Tuning granularity: updating the direction only for QKV and magnitude only for the other modules still beats LoRA at under half the parameters.
  number: LLaMA-7B 77.5 (0.39% params) against LoRA 74.7 (0.83%); LLaMA-13B 81.3 (0.31%) against LoRA 80.5 (0.67%). Text says "2.8%" and "0.8%" gains for the 78.1 / 81.5 versions of the comparison, not for the 77.5 / 81.3 rows.
  setup: Table 6, p9
  quote: "DoRA surpasses LoRA by 2.8% on LLaMA-7B and 0.8% on LLaMA-13B, while utilizing only less than half of the trainable parameters compared to LoRA."
  where: p9
- QDoRA (QLoRA with DoRA, run by Answer.AI, not the authors; reported as initial findings): it beats QLoRA and slightly exceeds full FT.
  number: +0.19 (LLaMA2-7B) and +0.23 (LLaMA3-8B) exact match over QLoRA. From Fig 6: QDoRA 0.56 and FT 0.51 (LLaMA2-7B?), QLoRA 0.32. Read from the figure axis text, order by model is uncertain.
  setup: 100k Orca-Math samples, 500 held out, exact-match metric, FSDP
  quote: "QDoRA not only significantly surpasses QLoRA by 0.19/0.23 on LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B, but it also slightly outperforms FT on both models, while using considerably less memory."
  where: p9
- Gradient analysis (Sec 4.2): the decomposition rescales and projects the gradient away from the current weight. The authors say this improves conditioning. The argument is a derivation under assumptions, not an empirical test.
  quote: "the weight gradient ∇W′L is scaled by m/||V′||c and is projected away from the current weight matrix."
  where: p4
- DoRA-tuned weights drift less from the pretrained weights than LoRA-tuned ones (LLaMA2-7B commonsense, Fig 3, p6). Text-to-image: DoRA gives better SDXL DreamBooth personalization on 3D-icon and Lego sets, judged qualitatively only (p10, Figs 10-11).

LIMITS
- Mostly one seed per cell, with no variance reported.
- The negative-correlation story is observational and rests on one case study (VL-BART). The authors only "suspect" the cause, and the claim that a negative correlation is "more optimal" is stated as a hypothesis.
- LLaMA2/3 LoRA baselines were rerun with the earlier hyperparameters, so they are not tuned independently. DoRA's learning rate was changed per model while LoRA's was not.
- Gains shrink where FT is already below LoRA (LLaVA).
- QDoRA results are third-party and initial.
- No cost comparison of DoRA against LoRA in time or memory. The LoRA-versus-DoRA gap in the rank sweep contains obvious failure cells.
- Future work named: audio and other domains beyond language and vision.
- Dated: the paper credits integration into Hugging Face PEFT.

BUILDS ON: LoRA (Hu et al., 2022); Weight Normalization (Salimans & Kingma, 2016), the magnitude/direction reparameterization; VeRA (Kopiczko et al., 2024); LLM-Adapters commonsense setup (Hu et al., 2023); Sung et al. 2022 (VL-BART setup); QLoRA (Dettmers et al., 2023); LLaVA (Liu et al., 2023a); Houlsby et al. 2019 and He et al. 2021 (adapters); Li & Liang 2021 (prefix).

CODE: none in the paper. The only formula worth keeping is Eq. 5 (p4): W' = m * (W0 + BA) / ||W0 + BA||_c, with column-wise norm and the norm detached from the graph per Eq. 11. Code link given: https://github.com/NVlabs/DoRA.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): DoRA overview. Pretrained weight is decomposed into magnitude (trainable) and direction (frozen, plus LoRA B,A), then merged. It is the best single diagram of what is trained and what merges.
- Fig 2 (p4): scatter of dM against dD for FT, LoRA and DoRA, query matrices. It shows the positive-versus-negative slope finding. Fig 7 (p14) is the same for V.
- Fig 5 (p8): average accuracy against rank for LoRA and DoRA, LLaMA-7B. Fig 3 (p6): drift from pretrained weights. Fig 6 (p9): QDoRA results.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. Figure text in the extraction is partly scrambled, such as axis labels in Fig 2 and 6. Fig 6 values are therefore uncertain, and I did not use them as claims.
